title: Critical convergence and Hausdorff measures for generalized Flint Hills series
summary: We study the generalized Flint Hills series $\mathcal{F}_{s,t}(x)=\sum_{n\ge1} n^{-s}|\sin(πnx)|^{-t}$ for $s>0$ and $t>1$. An explicit comparison with a series over continued-fraction denominators yields the Hausdorff dimension $\min\{1,2t/(s+t)\}$ of its divergence set. At each critical exponent $τ=1+s/t>2$ we construct numbers of irrationality exponent $τ$ realizing both convergence and divergence; the convergent examples establish Meiburg's conjecture in the range $t>1$. Both parts of the critical fibre have Hausdorff dimension $2/τ$. For $s>t$ and $h_κ(r)=r^{2/τ}(\log(1/r))^κ$ we prove…
